extraction.Name: Alice Brown Larvie
extraction.Cancelled: application of Alice Brown Larvie for cancelation of forced patent in fee
extraction.Refused/Protested: I got it thru the mail and just kept it, made no protest becuase I thot it was legal requirement of the U.S. Government, and the patent was already recorded without my knowledge
extraction.Recorded patent: the patent was already recorded without my knowledge, and I do not know who record the same
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: The was taken by foreclosure, sold by sheriff
extraction.Buyer: foreclosed by Bank of Ipswich, Ipswich, Edmunds Co. So. Dak.; H.E. Beebe was Vice President of the Bank of Ipswich who notified her land would be sold for the $500.00 owed; Buell & Denu of Rapid City, So. Dak. were the attorneys done the business for the Ipswich Bank
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: There were some taxes due so I was obliged mortgaged all of my allotment for five ($500.00) hundred dollars and paid the said taxes and used the balance for my support; the mortgage was foreclosed and redemption period closed on July 20, 1923
extraction.Occupation/Income: I am now supported by my husbond partly and I take in washing and help to support myself to a certain extent, and no assistance from the Federal Government nor from the State
extraction.NOTES: Mental conditions good, health good, financial conditions very poor; has three children depending upon husband and herself; did not receive any money from the foreclosure sale — land taken by law to satisfy the $500.00 mortgage and interest; I did not get what my land was worth; document is a questionnaire responding to 13 questions per instructions in letter from Supt. E. W. Jermark, Pine Ridge, dated November 9, 1928; notarized February 25, 1929
